Read 0-174.88 and catalogue (no chapters; embeddable; thumbnail URL available but no frame-based evidence). It is not exceptional enough to justify weak visual value. Reject this cut; choose a clear signaled all-or-nothing diagram/example rather than extending into the unrelated server demonstration.

Read 70.32-291.48 and catalogue (only Introduction chapter 0-380; embeddable). At 104.12-139.24 he defines cache-aside as an application-controlled cache beside the database. At 139.24-171.80 the profile request checks Redis, misses and queries the database; at 174.12-197.88 it stores a copy in Redis then responds. At 203.96-227.40 the next request hits Redis and returns without the database query. This explicitly supports f2 and matches Redis's cache-aside Python documentation. Drop proposed f1: a copied database result is illustrated, but primary-store authority rather than cache authority is never explained. Repeated-read benefit is covered at 233.44-259.96, but staleness eligibility and key construction f3/f4 are not taught. Use 105-259: the cache-aside heading starts around 104, and the following change/freshness discussion begins around 260 with invalidation at 283.24; it is excluded, so blocked cache.freshness_policy is not needed. No drawing or screen cues establish actual visuals; catalogue thumbnail existence alone is not proof. Nevertheless approve under the conceptual talking-head exception: this unusually clear, locally introduced profile example explicitly labels miss and hit, walks every actor and step in order and contrasts first versus repeated requests. The low visual score records the uncertainty, not a claim of whiteboard footage. Sweeping speed language is illustrative, not a guarantee for every workload.

Read 1375.44-1499.68 and catalogue Autogenerating migrations chapter 1207-1708. At 1409.52-1428.64 he reads documentation describing database-to-table-metadata comparison with the autogenerate option; 1427.36-1447.52 describes candidate migration files and developer review/modification before upgrade. At 1442.32-1468.88 he explains supplying Base.metadata in env.py, then resumes the earlier configured environment. The statements are correct against Alembic's autogeneration documentation and screen/documentation cues give plausible visual support; no prerequisite leak is established. However the sole claimed f3 includes the essential limitation that autogenerate cannot reliably infer schema intent such as table/column renames. The clip never teaches any detection limitation or rename/drop-add hazard, whereas the source explicitly warns autogenerate is not perfect and requires review/correction. Thus this is partial manual-review instruction, not a confirmed complete f3; neither command-with-message f2 nor any other full required fact is taught. Reject as fact mismatch rather than falsely marking f3 covered. A replacement range must explain a concrete detection limitation alongside candidate review, or revise the upstream fact/segment coverage design to represent this narrower teaching separately. Tightening to the documentation paragraph cannot supply the missing content.
